diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consequently, the entire transformed integrand is bounded near the boundary.

Unbounded integrands do not satisfy the assumptions of the Koksma--Hlawka error bound (i.e., the variation of the integrand in the sense of Hardy and Krause is infinite); thus, the rate of convergence of RQMC may deteriorate.

issues.failure_explanation: The derivations generally control only whether the ratio of the characteristic function to the proposal density is bounded or decays at the boundary. Boundedness is not sufficient for finite Hardy--Krause variation or for the derivative growth hypotheses needed for an O(N^{-1+epsilon}) RQMC rate, especially because inverse-CDF derivatives themselves diverge at the boundary. No theorem or derivative analysis bridges this gap, so the claimed rate guarantee is unsupported; the numerical experiments provide only empirical evidence.

failure_location.quote: Then, we tune the parameters of the proposal density to satisfy the derived boundary growth conditions that ensure nearly optimal convergence rates.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must prove suitable mixed-derivative or variation bounds for each transformed integrand and then invoke an RQMC theorem under matching hypotheses, or weaken the rate and regularity statements to empirical observations.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's advertised theoretical guarantee that its parameter rules preserve sufficient regularity and ensure nearly optimal RQMC convergence is not established. The empirical performance comparisons are not by themselves invalidated.
issues.title: Boundary boundedness does not establish the advertised RQMC convergence rates
issues.why_classification: Without a new regularity and convergence argument, the central theoretical guarantee must be withdrawn rather than locally corrected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consequently, the statistical error of the MC and RQMC methods is an upper bound; thus, the CPU times for the MC and RQMC methods are conservative because, in practice, they converge faster with respect to the exact relative error.

issues.failure_explanation: After replacing the undefined Q^{RQMC}_{N,d} by the replicate mean, the formula is C_alpha times an estimated standard error based on S randomized replicates. It is neither the root mean squared error itself nor a deterministic upper bound. Its confidence interpretation additionally requires an approximation such as a normal or Student-t calibration, which is not supplied. Thus the stopping rule does not justify the claimed upper-bound or conservative-runtime interpretation.

issues.overall_effect: The reported statistical errors and runtime stopping comparisons lack the stated RMSE and upper-bound guarantee, although the underlying randomized estimates can still be used with an explicitly approximate uncertainty analysis.
issues.title: Sample confidence half-width is presented as the RMSE and as an upper bound
issues.why_classification: The estimator can be retained, but its statistical interpretation and downstream stopping-time comparisons require substantive recalibration and qualification.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\boldsymbol{u} \mapsto \Psi(\boldsymbol{u}; \boldsymbol{\Lambda})$ is the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of some $\mathbb{R}^d$-valued RV with parameter vector $\boldsymbol{\Lambda}$ (e.g., mean, scale, and degrees of freedom), and $\Psi^{-1}(\boldsymbol{u}; \boldsymbol{\Lambda})$ is the ICDF.

issues.failure_explanation: A multivariate CDF is scalar-valued, not a bijection from R^d to [0,1]^d, and therefore has no vector inverse with Jacobian 1/psi as used here. The displayed change of variables is valid only after specifying an actual transport from independent uniforms to the target distribution, such as a Rosenblatt map or a model-specific mixture/factor construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the multivariate-CDF inverse by an explicitly defined almost-everywhere invertible transport with pushforward density psi, and derive the Jacobian identity. State separately when componentwise inverse CDFs, linear Gaussian factors, or mixture representations implement that transport.
issues.overall_effect: The general domain-transformation formulation is ill-defined for dependent proposal distributions. The later Gaussian and mixture constructions may furnish valid transports independently, but they do not make the stated general CDF inversion valid.
issues.title: A multivariate CDF is incorrectly treated as an invertible vector change of variables
issues.why_classification: The model-specific constructions offer a route to repair, but the general framework needs a nontrivial reformulation in terms of transport maps rather than a notational edit.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: From \eqref{eq:vg_conditions}, an appropriate choice of the parameter $\tilde{\nu}$ satisfies either the condition in Case (ii) or (iii), where (ii) implicitly relies on the constraint $ \frac{2T}{ \nu } -1 > 0$, which, if not satisfied, implies that the characteristic function is not integrable

issues.failure_explanation: If 2T/nu-1 is negative, the recommended floor gives tilde-nu=1, which is strictly greater than the critical value. The paper's own asymptotic calculation therefore places this recommendation in the divergent case, not in either admissible case. Any rescue would have to use payoff-transform decay and would require payoff-specific analysis absent from the proposed model-only rule.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the stated model-only VG rule to parameter regimes where a positive tilde-nu satisfying the derived inequality exists, or provide a new payoff-dependent tail analysis and parameter rule for the remaining regimes.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised VG domain-transformation prescription has no established boundary-control guarantee in the short-maturity regime; analogous feasibility problems occur for the dependent rule when 2T/nu-d is nonpositive.
issues.title: The short-maturity VG recommendation necessarily violates the derived boundary condition
issues.why_classification: Repair requires either excluding a meaningful parameter regime or adding a contained but nontrivial payoff-dependent analysis; the existing floor cannot be fixed by routine algebra.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consequently, we constructed the matrix $\boldsymbol{\tilde{\Sigma}}$ by setting $\boldsymbol{\tilde{\Sigma}} = \boldsymbol{P} \diag(\frac{2}{\lambda_1 \delta^2 T^2}, \ldots, \frac{2}{\lambda_d \delta^2 T^2} ) \boldsymbol{P}^{-1} = \frac{2}{ \delta^2 T^2 } \boldsymbol{\Delta}^{-1}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The Bessel asymptotic displayed by the paper contains a polynomial prefactor. Since v=(2-d)/2, the multivariate Laplace density behaves, apart from its exponential, like q^{(1-d)/4}, where q=y' tilde-Sigma^{-1}y. At the proposed equality matrix the exponential factors cancel, so the characteristic-function-to-density ratio grows like q^{(d-1)/4} for d>1 rather than tending to the stated constant. The derivation incorrectly keeps only the exponential terms.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the full polynomial Bessel prefactor. A source-supported sufficient workaround is to choose a strict matrix inequality so exponential decay dominates the polynomial growth; the equality/minimal-determinant recommendation must be abandoned or supplemented by payoff-specific decay conditions.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed boundedness of the NIG ratio and the recommended minimal-determinant dependent-asset transformation are false in dimensions greater than one. Payoff decay may rescue particular examples, but the stated model-only boundary guarantee does not.
issues.title: The multivariate NIG equality rule drops a polynomial tail factor
issues.why_classification: A comparable transformation survives by moving to a strict inequality, but the proposed optimal equality choice and its analysis must be materially changed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\{W_1(t),\dots, W_d(t)\}$ denotes independent standard Brownian motion

issues.failure_explanation: Conditionally on the common subordinator, the displayed dynamics with independent standard Brownian motions have Gaussian quadratic form z'z and drift beta'z. They cannot produce the Delta-dependent quadratic form (beta+iz)'Delta(beta+iz) used in the characteristic function unless the Brownian loading and drift are changed. Moreover, with a common inverse-Gaussian clock whose parameters depend on the full vector beta and Delta, the martingale correction generally depends on that common parameter, not only on beta_i as in the univariate formula. Thus the dynamics, characteristic function, and claimed martingale correction are mutually incompatible for the stated multivariate model.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must specify Gaussian loadings and subordinated drift consistent with Delta, derive the resulting joint characteristic function, and recompute the componentwise martingale corrections, or restrict the model and all claims to a compatible special case.
issues.overall_effect: The dependent multivariate NIG pricing model is not coherently defined, so the interpretation of the NIG Fourier integrands and general-Delta numerical methodology as risk-neutral option pricing is unreliable.
